In August 2010, the Yemeni army began a siege against militants linked to al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) who took control of the city of Lawdar in Abyan Governorate, Yemen. The siege was in response to an AQAP ambush on 20 August which killed 11 soldiers in the city. The siege was lifted by 24 August, with Yemeni forces successfully taking back the city. A total of 33 people were killed in the battle, 19 of them being AQAP militants.
Battle
On 19 August, two Yemeni soldiers were killed and three were injured in Lawdar by AQAP gunmen who opened fire on them with automatic weapons while in a souk and then proceeded to escape. Yemeni authorities subsequently tightened security measures across Abyan and began hunting the perpetrators. On 20 August, AQAP gunmen ambushed a security patrol in Lawdar, killing 11 Yemeni soldiers. Yemeni forces fired heavy artillery at the militants, killing two and injuring 20, while destroying several houses in the area.
In response to the ambush, the Yemeni government sent a large contingent of soldiers to besiege the city. The operation was being led directly by Defense Minister Gen. Mohammed Nasser Ahmed. Over the weekend on 21 and 22 August, the Yemeni Army distributed pamphlets around the city urging civilians to flee. Reports claimed that foreign fighters, primarily from Saudi Arabia and Pakistan were fighting alongside AQAP within the city.
Seven suspected AQAP fighters, including three foreigners of unknown nationalities, were killed in clashes with Yemeni forces on 21 August. On 22 August, the Yemeni government gave the militants a 24 hour ultimatum to leave the Lawdar or else the houses they were using would be bombed. Thousands of residents from the city fled after the ultimatum was issued, and intense fighting began again that night after the militants resisted against government forces. A total of seven AQAP fighters were killed during the day.
AQAP forces began withdrawing its forces from Lawdar on 23 August after transporting their wounded out of the city. Yemeni forces raided several houses which militants had barricaded themselves in, where they found larges stashes of weapons which included heavy weaponry such as rockets and anti-tank weapons. Four AQAP fighters along with three civilians were killed during the day. Among those killed included Adel Saleh Hardaba, AQAP's second in-command in the city.
Most of Lawdar's 80,000 residents had fled the city by 24 August according to the government. By the afternoon of 24 August, Yemeni officials reported that the army had entered Lawdar and had retaken control over most of the city. By late noon, the Yemeni Interior Ministry claimed to have taken full control over Lawdar, with Gen. Saleh al-Zaweri stating that security forces had "stormed the dens of the terrorists" in the city and were now "chasing the runaway elements". An AFP tally based on official and medical sources placed the total death count at 33; 11 soldiers, 19 militants and three civilians.
